source_refs.note: Exercise 12.2, Question 3: continuity at x = 2 and x = -2 (book p.233). Answer key PDF 310 labels the two answers (i), (ii) and wrongly says discontinuous at x = 2.

blocks.prompt: 3 If \[f(x) = \begin{cases} 3x, & x \le -2 \\ x^2 - 1, & -2 < x < 2 \\ 3, & x \ge 2 \end{cases}\]discuss continuity at \(x = 2\) and \(x = -2\).
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein ek hi function ko do points par check karna hai: \(x = 2\) aur \(x = -2\). Yeh dono woh jagah hain jahan formula badalta hai.
Har point ka faisla alag hota hai; ek point par continuous hona doosre ke baare mein kuch nahi batata.
Plan: (a) \(x = 2\) par \(f(2)\), LHL, RHL; (b) phir \(x = -2\) par yahi kaam.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(x \le -2\) ke liye \(f(x) = 3x\), \(-2 < x < 2\) ke liye \(f(x) = x^2 - 1\), aur \(x \ge 2\) ke liye \(f(x) = 3\).
Humein find karna hai: \(x = 2\) aur \(x = -2\) par continuity.
Tareeqa: \(f\) point \(x = c\) par continuous (lagataar, bina toote) tab hota hai jab teen shartein poori hon: (i) \(f(c)\) defined ho, (ii) \(\lim_{x \to c} f(x)\) exist kare yani LHL = RHL, (iii) yeh limit \(f(c)\) ke barabar ho. Agar ek bhi shart toot jaye to \(f\) wahan discontinuous hai. Aasaan zubaan mein: graph ko us point par qalam uthaye baghair bana sakein to continuous.

(a) \(x = 2\) par: \(f(2)\) nikalein
\[f(2) = 3\]
Kyun: Teesre tukre ke saath \(x \ge 2\) hai, yani 2 khud is mein shamil hai. Yeh constant function hai, is liye value seedhi 3.

(a) 2 par left hand limit
\[\lim_{x \to 2^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 2^-} (x^2 - 1)\]
\[= 4 - 1 = 3\]
Kyun: 2 se zara pehle (1.9, 1.99) hum \(-2 < x < 2\) wale beech ke tukre mein hain, jis ka formula \(x^2 - 1\) hai.

(a) 2 par right hand limit
\[\lim_{x \to 2^+} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 2^+} 3 = 3\]
Kyun: 2 ke baad function hamesha 3 hai. Constant ki limit wahi constant hoti hai, chahe \(x\) kahin bhi jaye.

(a) \(x = 2\) ka faisla
\[\text{LHL} = \text{RHL} = 3 = f(2)\]
Kyun: Teeno shartein poori: \(f(2)\) defined, limit exist karti hai, aur limit \(= f(2)\). Is liye \(f\) point \(x = 2\) par continuous hai. Parabola ki curve bilkul usi height 3 par pohanchti hai jahan se seedhi flat line shuru hoti hai.

(b) \(x = -2\) par: \(f(-2)\) nikalein
\[f(-2) = 3(-2) = -6\]
Kyun: Pehle tukre ke saath \(x \le -2\) hai, is liye \(-2\) pehle tukre \(3x\) mein aata hai.

(b) \(-2\) par left hand limit
\[\lim_{x \to -2^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to -2^-} 3x\]
\[= -6\]
Kyun: \(-2\) se left (jaise \(-2.01\), jo \(-2\) se chhota hai) pehla tukra \(3x\) chalta hai.

(b) \(-2\) par right hand limit
\[\lim_{x \to -2^+} f(x) = \lim_{x \to -2^+} (x^2 - 1)\]
\[= (-2)^2 - 1 = 3\]
Kyun: \(-2\) se right (jaise \(-1.99\)) hum beech ke tukre mein hain.
Dhyan dein: \((-2)^2 = +4\) hota hai, \(-4\) nahi. Bracket lagaye baghair \(-2^2\) likhne se yahi ghalti hoti hai.

(b) \(x = -2\) ka faisla
\[\text{LHL} = -6\]
\[\text{RHL} = 3\]
\[-6 \ne 3\]
Kyun: Left aur right limits alag hain, is liye \(\lim_{x \to -2} f(x)\) exist hi nahi karti. Doosri shart toot gayi, aur ek shart ka tootna hi discontinuity ke liye kaafi hai. Graph yahan \(-6\) se seedha 3 par chhalaang (jump) lagata hai.

Tasdeeq
\[f(1.99) = 3.9601 - 1 = 2.9601\]
\[f(-2.01) = -6.03,\ f(-1.99) = 2.9601\]
Kyun: 2 ke dono taraf values 3 ke qareeb hain (continuous), jabke \(-2\) ke dono taraf values bohat door door hain (jump). Calculator se yeh check bilkul wazeh kar deta hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(f\) point \(x = 2\) par continuous hai aur \(x = -2\) par discontinuous hai

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key mein "(i) \(f\) is discontinuous at \(x = 2\)" likha hai. Yeh ghalat hai: \(x = 2\) par left hand limit \(2^2 - 1 = 3\), right hand limit 3 aur \(f(2) = 3\) hai, is liye \(f\) wahan continuous hai. Key ka "(ii) \(f\) is discontinuous at \(x = -2\)" sahi hai.
